verdicts.title: Karchmer-Wigderson Games for Hazard-free Computation
verdicts.abstract_excerpt:
We present a Karchmer-Wigderson game to study the complexity of hazard-free formulas. This new game is both a generalization of the monotone Karchmer-Wigderson game and an analog of the classical Boolean Karchmer-Wigderson game. Therefore, it acts as a bridge between the existing monotone and general games.

verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract introduces a Karchmer-Wigderson game for hazard-free formulas as a bridge between monotone and general KW games, but says nothing about Stanley-Reisner rings, projective dimension, or Hochster's formula bounding monotone-KW depth.

verdicts.title: Adaptive Lower Bound for Testing Monotonicity on the Line
verdicts.abstract_excerpt:
In the property testing model, the task is to distinguish objects possessing some property from the objects that are far from it. One of such properties is monotonicity, when the objects are functions from one poset to another. This is an active area of research. verdicts.title: Multiparty Karchmer-Wigderson Games and Threshold Circuits
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: We suggest a generalization of Karchmer-Wigderson communication games to the multiparty setting. Our generalization turns out to be tightly connected to circuits consisting of threshold gates. This allows us to obtain new explicit constructions of such circuits for several functions. In particular, we provide an explicit (polynomial-time computable) log-depth monotone formula for Majority function, consisting only of 3-bit majority gates and variables. This resolves a conjecture of Cohen et al.
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract concerns a multiparty generalization of Karchmer-Wigderson games for threshold circuits and an explicit log-depth majority formula, with no mention of Stanley-Reisner rings, projective dimension, or homology-based lower bounds on monotone-KW depth.
